issues.description: Removal of `category__in` from DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES regresses active-filter badge display
issues.detail: The diff adds a Category filter to the findings page but removes the `category__in` entry from `DEFAULT_FILTER_BADGES`. Unless a replacement is registered elsewhere (not shown in the diff), selected categories will no longer surface as active-filter badges — breaking the established UX for all other filters and the PR's own 'Active Filter Badges' goal.

issues.description: Category filter values aren't formatted in active badge / selected chips path
issues.detail: `labelFormatter` is only applied inside `DataTableFilterCustom`'s list rendering. Selected-chip rendering, badge label outside the dropdown, and any URL-driven display of active categories will still show raw IDs like `internet-exposed` instead of `Internet Exposed`, producing inconsistent labels across the UI.

issues.description: Short-word acronym heuristic mislabels real words like 'web', 'app', 'log', 'key'
issues.detail: `formatWord` upper-cases any word with length ≤ 3, so future categories such as `web-exposed`, `app-secrets`, `log-retention`, or `key-management` would render as `WEB Exposed`, `APP Secrets`, etc. Given that the prior explicit mapping was removed, this heuristic is the sole source of truth and is fragile for an evolving API-provided category list.

Adding `Info: 4` alongside `Informational: 4` creates two entries that sort identically. If the rest of the codebase keys on a single canonical severity string, ordering and grouping become non-deterministic when both forms appear in the same dataset. Prefer a normalization step that maps `Info` -> `Informational` upstream.

`handleValueChange` checks `value === "" || value === "all"`, but Radix `Select` disallows empty-string `SelectItem` values and only `all` is rendered. The empty-string branch can never trigger; remove it to avoid implying a code path that doesn't exist.

`Math.max(...data.map(d => d.value))` is computed for every row in the render loop. For typical category counts this is negligible, but it should be hoisted above the `.map` callback for clarity and to avoid O(n^2) work as the chart scales.

review.summary: The PR introduces a Risk Radar component, a shared `getCategoryLabel` utility, and a new Category filter on the findings page, alongside a Threat Score -> ThreatScore rename. The most consequential issues are a regression in active-filter badge handling (the `category__in` badge config was removed without an obvious replacement) and inconsistent label formatting because `labelFormatter` is only wired into one render path. The category-label heuristic is also fragile now that the explicit mapping was deleted — any future 3-letter category that isn't an acronym will be mis-rendered. Minor concerns include a duplicate `SEVERITY_ORDER` value, dead code in the selector, and an O(n^2) computation in the bar chart.
